why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The API now requires a bearer key with viewer, cook or manager roles, and `npm test` (29 pass) and `npm run lint` both pass. `data/db.json` has no keys yet, so I left it alone. Once it migrates to schema 3 on load, every request will get 401 until you add keys to it. I added one key per role to `data/seed.json`.

- **Roles:** viewer can GET only. Cook can also POST cook, waste, temperatures and stock-take counts. Manager can do everything.
- **Errors:** I added `unauthorized` (401) and `forbidden` (403) with English messages, and I didn't add Korean ones.
- **Audit:** every non-GET request made with a known key is logged, whatever its status (including 403 and 409 results). Requests with a missing or unknown key aren't logged, because there's no key name to record. `GET /audit` is manager-only and lists newest first.
- **Schema 3:** the keys and the audit log live in the data as `apiKeys` and `audit`, so I bumped the schema to 3 and added a 2→3 migration. Migrated files start with no keys and an empty audit log.
- **Tests:** `tests/helpers.js` now sends the manager key by default, so the existing tests send a key without edits to each call. I changed two assertions in `tests/cli.test.js` from schema 2 to 3. I also added `tests/auth.test.js`, which you didn't ask for, to cover 401, 403 and the audit log.
- **Docs:** README (new Access section, `GET /audit` under Routes), `docs/API.md`, `docs/DATA.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.
